<!-- head-1: body_md -->
\;{\rm (see Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-test} for details)} \emph{Let $A$ be an $n$-Igusa--Todorov Artin algebra with witness $V$, and put $t=t(V)$. If $M\in{}^{\perp}A$ and}
\[
\operatorname{Ext}_A^q(M,M)=0\quad(1\leq q\leq2t+1),
\]
\emph{then $M$ is projective. Consequently, every Igusa--Todorov Artin algebra satisfies the Auslander--Reiten conjecture.}
\vskip 5pt
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
\; {\rm  (see Proposition~\ref{prop:repdim} for details)}~ \emph{Every Artin algebra of representation dimension at most three satisfies the Auslander--Reiten conjecture.}
\vskip 5pt
<!-- end head-2 -->
<!-- head-3: body_md -->
\; {\rm (see Proposition~\ref{prop:radical-IT} and Corollary~\ref{cor:radical})}~ \emph{Let $A$ be an Artin algebra with radical $J$. If $J^{2m+1}=0$ and $A/J^m$ has finite representation type for some $m\geq1$, then $A$ satisfies the Auslander--Reiten conjecture. In particular, every Artin algebra with radical cube zero satisfies the conjecture.}
\vskip 5pt
<!-- end head-3 -->
<!-- defn-1: body_md -->
\label{def:IT}
Let $n\geq0$ be an integer. The algebra $A$ is \emph{$n$-Igusa--Todorov} if there is a module $V$ such that every module $Y$ admits an exact sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow V_1\longrightarrow V_0\longrightarrow\Omega^nY\longrightarrow0,
\quad V_0,V_1\in\operatorname{add} V.
\]
We call $V$ an \emph{$n$-Igusa--Todorov witness}. An algebra is \emph{Igusa--Todorov} if it is $n$-Igusa--Todorov for some $n$.
<!-- end defn-1 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:syzygy}
Let $X\in{}^{\perp}A$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Omega^aX\in{}^{\perp}A$ for every $a\geq0$.
\item For $a\geq0$ and $q\geq1$,
\[
\operatorname{Ext}_A^q(\Omega^aX,\Omega^aX)\simeq\operatorname{Ext}_A^q(X,X).
\]
\item For $a\geq1$ and every module $Y$,
\[
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(\Omega^aX,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Ext}_A^a(X,Y).
\]
\item If $\operatorname{pd}_A X<\infty$, then $X$ is projective.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The first assertion follows by dimension shifting. Let
\[
0\longrightarrow\Omega X\longrightarrow P\longrightarrow X\longrightarrow0
\]
be a projective cover sequence. Every finitely generated projective module belongs to $\operatorname{add} A$. Hence $X\in{}^{\perp}A$ gives $\operatorname{Ext}_A^{>0}(X,P)=0$. Dimension shifting in the two variables now gives, for $q\geq1$,
\[
\operatorname{Ext}_A^q(\Omega X,\Omega X)
\simeq\operatorname{Ext}_A^{q+1}(X,\Omega X)
\simeq\operatorname{Ext}_A^q(X,X).
\]
Iteration proves (2).

For (3), the long exact sequence associated to the projective cover of $\Omega^{a-1}X$ identifies $\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(\Omega^{a-1}X,Y)$ with the quotient of $\operatorname{Hom}_A(\Omega^aX,Y)$ by the morphisms that extend to that projective cover. These morphisms factor through a projective module. Conversely, if a morphism factors as $\Omega^aX\to Q\to Y$ with $Q$ projective, its first factor extends to the cover because
\[
\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(\Omega^{a-1}X,Q)\simeq\operatorname{Ext}_A^a(X,Q)=0.
\]
The quotient is therefore stable Hom, and dimension shifting proves (3).

For (4), suppose that $\operatorname{pd}_A X=d>0$. Then $\Omega^dX$ is projective and
\[
\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(\Omega^{d-1}X,\Omega^dX)
\simeq\operatorname{Ext}_A^d(X,\Omega^dX)=0.
\]
The projective cover sequence of $\Omega^{d-1}X$ splits, making $\Omega^{d-1}X$ projective, contrary to the choice of $d$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:no-proj-summand}
If $X\in{}^{\perp}A$, then $\Omega X$ has no nonzero projective direct summand.
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Write $0\to\Omega X\xrightarrow{u}P\to X\to0$ for its projective cover sequence. If a projective module $Q$ is a direct summand of $\Omega X$, the projection $\pi:\Omega X\to Q$ extends to $\widetilde\pi:P\to Q$, because $\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(X,Q)=0$. The composite of the inclusion $Q\to\Omega X\xrightarrow{u}P$ with $\widetilde\pi$ is $1_Q$. Thus the image of $Q$ is a direct summand of $P$ contained in $\operatorname{rad} P$. If $P=Q\oplus P'$ with this copy of $Q$, then $\operatorname{rad} P=\operatorname{rad} Q\oplus\operatorname{rad} P'$, and hence $Q=\operatorname{rad} Q$. Nakayama's lemma gives $Q=0$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:finite-range}
Let $M\in{}^{\perp}A$, let $N\geq1$ be an integer, and suppose that $\operatorname{Ext}_A^q(M,M)=0$ for $1\leq q\leq N$. Fix an integer $d\geq1$ and set $X_i=\Omega^{d+i}M$ for $i\geq0$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\operatorname{Ext}_A^q(X_i,X_i)=0$ for $1\leq q\leq N$;
\item $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(X_a,X_b)=0$ if $1\leq a-b\leq N$;
\item $\operatorname{Ext}_A^q(X_a,X_b)=0$ if $a\geq b$, $q\geq1$, and $q+a-b\leq N$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Part (1) is \cref{lem:syzygy}(2). For $a>b$, part (3) of that lemma gives
\[
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(X_a,X_b)\simeq\operatorname{Ext}_A^{a-b}(X_b,X_b).
\]
For $a\geq b$ and $q\geq1$, dimension shifting gives
\[
\operatorname{Ext}_A^q(X_a,X_b)\simeq\operatorname{Ext}_A^{q+a-b}(X_b,X_b).
\]
These identities prove the remaining assertions.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:pullback}
Consider exact sequences
\[
0\longrightarrow K\xrightarrow{v}L\xrightarrow{p}X\longrightarrow0,
\quad
\varepsilon\colon~~~0\longrightarrow Y\xrightarrow{u}P\xrightarrow{\pi}X\longrightarrow0,
\]
where $P$ is projective. If the image of $[\varepsilon]$ in $\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(L,Y)$ under pullback along $p$ is zero, then
\[
L\oplus Y\simeq K\oplus P.
\]
In particular, if $K,L\in\operatorname{add} V$ and $A\in\operatorname{add} V$, then $Y\in\operatorname{add} V$.
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
The pullback splits if and only if $p$ lifts to a morphism $h:L\to P$ with $\pi h=p$. There is then a morphism $g:K\to Y$ such that $ug=hv$. The sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow K\xrightarrow{(v,-g)}L\oplus Y
\xrightarrow{(h,u)}P\longrightarrow0
\]
is exact. Surjectivity follows by first lifting the image in $X$ through $p$. The description of the kernel follows from $\ker p=\operatorname{Im} v$ and $\ker\pi=\operatorname{Im} u$. It splits because $P$ is projective. The last assertion follows since $\operatorname{add} V$ is closed under direct summands.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:segment}
Let $M\in{}^{\perp}A$ be nonprojective, let $V$ be a module, and let $d,N\geq1$ be integers. Suppose that
\[
\operatorname{Ext}_A^q(M,M)=0\quad(1\leq q\leq N).
\]
Set $X_i=\Omega^{d+i}M$ for $0\leq i\leq N$. If, for every $0\leq i<N$, there is an exact sequence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:presentation}
0\longrightarrow K_i\longrightarrow L_i\xrightarrow{p_i}X_i\longrightarrow0,
\quad K_i,L_i\in\operatorname{add} V,
\end{equation}
then $N\leq2t(V)$.
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Replace $V$ by $V\oplus A$ and then by a basic module with the same additive closure. Write $t=t(V)$. Adding $A$ introduces only projective indecomposable summands, so this replacement preserves $t$. It also preserves the assumed presentations. Since $M$ is nonprojective, \cref{lem:syzygy}(4) gives $\operatorname{pd}_A M=\infty$. Every $X_i$ is consequently nonzero. Moreover, $d\geq1$ ensures that each $X_i$ is a positive syzygy of $M$. It follows from \cref{lem:syzygy,lem:no-proj-summand} that $X_i\in{}^{\perp}A$ and that $X_i$ has no nonzero projective direct summand. In particular, none of the $X_i$ is projective.

For $0\leq i<N$, write the projective cover extension as
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cover}
\varepsilon_i\colon ~~~
0\longrightarrow X_{i+1}\longrightarrow P_i\longrightarrow X_i\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
Since $X_i$ is not projective, $[\varepsilon_i]\neq0$. Denote the pullback map by
\[
\rho_i:\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(X_i,X_{i+1})\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(L_i,X_{i+1}).
\]
Partition the index set $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ as
\[
I=\{i\mid\rho_i([\varepsilon_i])=0\},\quad
II=\{i\mid\rho_i([\varepsilon_i])\neq0\}.
\]

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{\bf The indices in $I$.}
For $i\in I$, \cref{lem:pullback} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:support}
L_i\oplus X_{i+1}\simeq K_i\oplus P_i,
\quad\text{and hence }X_{i+1}\in\operatorname{add} V.
\end{equation}
If $i<j$ lie in $I$ and $X_{i+1}$ and $X_{j+1}$ have a common indecomposable summand $U$, the composite
\[
X_{j+1}\twoheadrightarrow U\hookrightarrow X_{i+1}
\]
has nonzero stable class. Indeed, a factorization of this composite through a projective module would, after composing with the corresponding inclusion and projection, factor $1_U$ through a projective module. This would make $U$ projective, a contradiction. But \cref{lem:finite-range}(2) gives
\[
\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(X_{j+1},X_{i+1})=0,
\quad 1\leq j-i\leq N-1.
\]
Thus the nonprojective supports of the modules $X_{i+1}$, $i\in I$, are nonempty and pairwise disjoint. By \eqref{eq:support}, they lie among the $t$ nonprojective summands of $V$. Therefore
$|I|\leq t.$

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{\bf The indices in $II$.}
Write $II=\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}$. If $q=0$, then $|II|\leq t$ is immediate, so suppose $q>0$. Define the integer matrix $C=(c_{ab})_{1\leq a,b\leq q}$ by
\[
c_{ab}=\ell_R\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(L_{i_a},X_{i_b+1})
-\ell_R\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(K_{i_a},X_{i_b+1}).
\]
For later use, applying $\operatorname{Hom}_A(-,Y)$ to \eqref{eq:presentation} gives the exact segment
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ext-segment}
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(X_i,Y)&\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(L_i,Y)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(K_i,Y)\\
&\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}_A^2(X_i,Y).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

If $a>b$, then $i_a\geq i_b+1$. For $r=1,2$, we have
\[
1\leq r+i_a-(i_b+1)\leq N.
\]
Indeed, $r+i_a-(i_b+1)\leq2+(N-1)-1=N$. Dimension shifting and \cref{lem:syzygy}(2) give
\[
\operatorname{Ext}_A^r(X_{i_a},X_{i_b+1})
\simeq\operatorname{Ext}_A^{r+i_a-i_b-1}(M,M)=0
\quad(r=1,2).
\]
The middle map in \eqref{eq:ext-segment}, with $i=i_a$ and $Y=X_{i_b+1}$, is therefore an isomorphism. This proves $c_{ab}=0$.

For the diagonal, apply $\operatorname{Hom}_A(X_i,-)$ to \eqref{eq:cover}. Since $X_i\in{}^{\perp}A$, we obtain
\[
\operatorname{Ext}_A^2(X_i,X_{i+1})\simeq\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(X_i,X_i)=0.
\]
Consequently, \eqref{eq:ext-segment} gives the short exact sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Im}\rho_i\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(L_i,X_{i+1})
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(K_i,X_{i+1})\longrightarrow0.
\]
Additivity of composition length yields
\[
c_{aa}=\ell_R(\operatorname{Im}\rho_{i_a})>0,
\]
where strict positivity follows from $i_a\in II$. Thus $C$ is upper triangular with positive diagonal, so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:full-rank}
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}C=q.
\end{equation}

Let $U_1,\cdots,U_t$ be representatives of the nonprojective indecomposable summands of $V$. By Krull--Schmidt, we may write
\[
L_i\simeq L_i^{\mathrm{pr}}\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha=1}^tU_\alpha^{\ell_{i\alpha}},
\quad
K_i\simeq K_i^{\mathrm{pr}}\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha=1}^tU_\alpha^{k_{i\alpha}},
\]
where $L_i^{\mathrm{pr}}$ and $K_i^{\mathrm{pr}}$ are projective. Since first Ext vanishes when its first argument is projective,
\[
c_{ab}=\sum_{\alpha=1}^t
(\ell_{i_a\alpha}-k_{i_a\alpha})\,
\ell_R\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(U_\alpha,X_{i_b+1}).
\]
Hence $C=DE$, where
\[
D=(\ell_{i_a\alpha}-k_{i_a\alpha})_{a,\alpha},
\quad
E=(\ell_R\operatorname{Ext}_A^1(U_\alpha,X_{i_b+1}))_{\alpha,b}
\]
have sizes $q\times t$ and $t\times q$, respectively. It follows that $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}C\leq t$. Together with \eqref{eq:full-rank}, this gives $|II|=q\leq t$. The same conclusion covers $t=0$, when the factorization forces $C=0$.

Combining the two counts proves
\[
N=|I|+|II|\leq2t,
\]
as required.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:finite-test}
Let $A$ be an $n$-Igusa--Todorov Artin algebra with witness $V$, and put $t=t(V)$. If $M\in{}^{\perp}A$ and
\[
\operatorname{Ext}_A^q(M,M)=0\quad(1\leq q\leq 2t+1),
\]
then $M$ is projective. Consequently, every Igusa--Todorov Artin algebra satisfies ARC.
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Suppose that $M$ is nonprojective and set $N=2t+1$. For each $0\leq i<N$, apply the $n$-Igusa--Todorov property to $Y=\Omega^{i+1}M$. This gives a presentation in $\operatorname{add} V$ of $\Omega^nY\simeq\Omega^{n+1+i}M$. Thus \cref{prop:segment} applies with $d=n+1$ and yields $2t+1=N\leq2t$, a contradiction. The case $t=0$ is included, since then $N=1$. Finally, the vanishing in \eqref{eq:ARC} implies the hypotheses of the finite test.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:selfinjective}
Let $A$ be a self-injective Igusa--Todorov Artin algebra with witness $V$. Every nonprojective module has a nonzero self-extension in some degree between $1$ and $2t(V)+1$. In particular, every self-orthogonal $A$-module is projective.
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Since $A$ is injective as a left module over itself, ${}^{\perp}A=A\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$. Apply \cref{thm:finite-test}.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:orthogonal-IT}
Suppose that there are an integer $n\geq0$ and a module $V$ such that every module $Y$ satisfying $\operatorname{Ext}_A^i(Y,Y\oplus A)=0$ for all $i>0$ admits an exact sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow V_1\longrightarrow V_0\longrightarrow\Omega^nY\longrightarrow0,
\quad V_0,V_1\in\operatorname{add} V.
\]
Then $A$ satisfies ARC.
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Put $t=t(V)$. If a nonprojective module $M$ satisfied the vanishing in \eqref{eq:ARC}, then every syzygy of $M$ would satisfy the same vanishing by \cref{lem:syzygy}. In particular, the assumed presentation is available for $Y=\Omega^{i+1}M$, $0\leq i\leq2t$. Applying \cref{prop:segment} with $d=n+1$ and $N=2t+1$ gives the contradiction $2t+1\leq2t$.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- rem-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:lat-IT}
The finite number of indecomposable isomorphism classes in $\operatorname{add} V$ is essential to both counts in the proof. Bravo, Lanzilotta, Mendoza and Vivero \cite[Definition~5.1]{BLMV2021} introduced Lat-Igusa--Todorov algebras, for which the additional summands may range over a subcategory with infinitely many indecomposable isomorphism classes. The argument therefore does not establish ARC for that larger class. In particular, \cref{cor:selfinjective} retains the Igusa--Todorov hypothesis.
<!-- end rem-1 -->
<!-- prop-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:repdim}
If $\operatorname{rep.dim} A\leq3$, then $A$ is $0$-Igusa--Todorov. Consequently, $A$ satisfies ARC.
<!-- end prop-3 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Choose a generator-cogenerator $G$ such that $\operatorname{gl.dim}\operatorname{End}_A(G)^{\mathrm{op}}\leq3$. Apply the characterization of Wei \cite[Lemma~2.1]{Wei2008} with parameter $1$. It gives an exact sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow G_1\longrightarrow G_0\longrightarrow X\longrightarrow0
\]
for every $X\inA\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$, where $G_0,G_1\in\operatorname{add} G$. Hence $G$ is a $0$-Igusa--Todorov witness. The second assertion follows from \cref{thm:finite-test}.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:radical-IT}
Let $J=\operatorname{rad} A$ and let $m\geq1$. Assume that $J^{2m+1}=0$ and $C=A/J^m$ has finite representation type. If $V$ is an additive generator of $C$-\textup{mod}, viewed as an $A$-module, then
\[
W=A\oplus V\oplus\Omega_A V
\]
is a $1$-Igusa--Todorov witness for $A$.
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Let $N\inA\text{-}\mathrm{mod}$ and set $X=\Omega_A N$. If $P\twoheadrightarrow N$ is its projective cover, then $X\subseteq JP$. Consequently,
\[
J^{2m}X\subseteq J^{2m+1}P=0.
\]
Put $U=J^mX$ and $Q=X/U$. Both $U$ and $Q$ are annihilated by $J^m$, so they are $C$-modules and hence belong to $\operatorname{add} V$.

Form the pullback of a projective cover $P_Q\twoheadrightarrow Q$ along $X\twoheadrightarrow Q$. Its middle module $E$ fits into exact sequences
\[
0\longrightarrow\Omega_AQ\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow X\longrightarrow0,
\quad
0\longrightarrow U\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow P_Q\longrightarrow0.
\]
The second sequence splits, so the first becomes
\[
0\longrightarrow\Omega_AQ\longrightarrow U\oplus P_Q
\longrightarrow\Omega_A N\longrightarrow0.
\]
Since $Q\in\operatorname{add} V$, there is a module $Q'$ and an integer $r\geq1$ such that $Q\oplus Q'\simeq V^r$. Taking projective covers gives
\[
\Omega_AQ\oplus\Omega_AQ'\simeq\Omega_A(V^r)\simeq(\Omega_AV)^r.
\]
Thus $\Omega_AQ\in\operatorname{add}(\Omega_AV)$. The two left terms therefore lie in $\operatorname{add} W$, as required.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:radical}
Under the hypotheses of \cref{prop:radical-IT}, let $t=t(A\oplus V\oplus\Omega_AV)$. If $M\in{}^{\perp}A$ and $\operatorname{Ext}_A^q(M,M)=0$ for $1\leq q\leq2t+1$, then $M$ is projective. In particular, $A$ satisfies ARC.
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Apply \cref{thm:finite-test} to the witness in \cref{prop:radical-IT}.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:cube-zero}
Every Artin algebra with radical cube zero satisfies ARC.
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Take $m=1$ in \cref{cor:radical}. The algebra $A/J$ is semisimple and therefore has finite representation type.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- rem-2: body_md -->
The generalized Nakayama conjecture and ARC are equivalent as assertions over all Artin algebras. This does not give a pointwise implication from the former to the latter, as explained by Chen, Hu, Qin and Wang \cite[Introduction]{CHQW2023}. The application concerning radical powers instead follows directly from the explicit Igusa--Todorov witness.
<!-- end rem-2 -->
